summary.headline: Sharp whipsaw reversal one session later (7/8): the chip/AI-infrastructure names that re-escalated to RED on 7/7's Samsung-driven selloff (MRVL, CRDO, LRCX, AMD) round-tripped back to green, alongside a broad semiconductor rally (NVDA, NXPI, QCOM, ADI, KEYS all up). New RED: SYF -9.64%, the sleeve's worst single-day move, on tier-1-confirmed (CNBC) 30-year Treasury yields holding above 5% pressuring consumer-finance funding costs ahead of SYF's 7/21 earnings — a direct materialization of its 'net interest margin pressure from higher funding costs' key_risk. AEM remains the lone persisting RED (Barnat guidance-cut risk still unresolved, formal update due 7/29, -3.65% today with no fresh catalyst). New/upgraded AMBER band: TOL -3.74% (margin compression, elevated mortgage-rate sensitivity), GPC -3.08% (O'Reilly's confirmed $10B NAPA bid still undecided, Bloomberg reports a decision possible 'late summer'), FCX -3.01% (second consecutive ~-3% session, no confirmed catalyst), CHD -2.84%, COIN -2.47% (crypto-tape softness — ETHA -2.74% and IBIT -2.48% also down), SUPV -2.2% (Argentina macro, ongoing), FTNT -1.21% (FortiBleed reporting still static). On the positive side: HUT +9.82% on $7.5B in confirmed project financing plus a wave of analyst price-target increases (Rosenblatt, B. Riley, Jefferies, KBW); VLO +6.28% on strong refining crack spreads ahead of its 7/30 print. CWAN roster issue persists a 10th consecutive run. TSM's 7/16 earnings (confirmed via TSMC investor relations) falls inside the 2-week hyperscaler-capex calendar watch.

flags.headline: SYF -9.64% — sleeve's worst single-day move, on confirmed 30-year Treasury yield pressure ahead of 7/21 earnings
flags.detail: Synchrony fell 9.64% ($75.52→$68.24) in the largest single-day decline in the book this run. The 30-year Treasury yield has been holding above the 5% level since 7/7 (CNBC, tier-1), a level last seen before the financial crisis, which pressures consumer-finance funding costs and valuations broadly. Secondary reporting (GuruFocus, TipRanks, MarketBeat) attributes the SYF-specific magnitude to a mix of broad risk-off trading and caution ahead of Synchrony's July 21 earnings, where Wall Street expects a double-digit EPS decline. This is a direct, thesis-relevant development, though the company-specific causal chain (vs. the macro yield move itself) rests on secondary sources — no company release or exchange notice found this run.
flags.thesis_link: Matches SYF key_risks: 'Revenue growth deceleration... suggests net interest margin pressure from higher funding costs' and 'Consumer credit cycle normalization... could compress earnings.' Rising long-end yields are a direct materialization of the funding-cost risk already identified in the screener report.

flags.headline: AEM -3.65% — persisting RED, Barnat guidance-cut risk still unresolved, formal update due 7/29
flags.detail: AEM pulled back 3.65% with no fresh catalyst found this run. The lone open thesis risk — a possible Barnat guidance cut — remains unresolved with a formal update still expected 2026-07-29. No new regulatory or Indigenous-consultation development found in this run's search (contrary to language carried in the report's static key_risks text, which describes a standing/background risk, not a new event).
flags.thesis_link: Matches AEM key_risk: 'Forward PEG of 2.12 indicates the stock is priced for continued gold price strength and production growth — any execution miss... could trigger meaningful valuation compression.' Held at RED on persistence of the unresolved Barnat catalyst, not on today's move alone.

flags.detail: Toll Brothers fell 3.74%. No single new news item found; consistent with the stock's existing margin/rate-sensitivity thesis risk.
flags.thesis_link: Matches TOL key_risk: 'Luxury homebuilding is acutely sensitive to interest rate and wealth effects — sustained elevated mortgage rates... could simultaneously reduce demand and compress pricing.'

flags.headline: GPC -3.08% — O'Reilly's confirmed $10B NAPA bid still undecided, decision possible 'late summer'
flags.detail: GPC fell 3.08%. O'Reilly Automotive's $10B cash bid for GPC's NAPA automotive unit was confirmed by Bloomberg on 7/2; GPC has not announced a decision and could retain the business, proceed with its planned spinoff, or accept the bid, with a decision potentially landing by late summer 2026. No decision this run — upgraded from prior INFO to AMBER given the size of today's move and the approaching decision window.
flags.thesis_link: Matches GPC key_risk: 'Business separation execution risk — $225-250M in transformation costs, management distraction, and Moody's negative outlook create uncertainty around whether the breakup will actually unlock value or destroy it.'

flags.thesis_link: Matches FCX key_risk: 'Copper price cyclicality — a correction... would slash EBITDA by 40%+ and stress the... capex program.'
